text: I do not mean by this to recommend to you 'le fade doucereux', the insipid softness of a gentle fool; no, assert your own opinion, oppose other people's when wrong; but let your manner, your air, your terms, and your tone of voice, be soft and gentle, and that easily and naturally, not affectedly.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CXLI, to his son, London, May 6, Old Style 1751
